source: Shem Tov Hebrew Matthew (Even Bochan, Ibn Shaprut c. 1385; critical text ed. G. Howard, base ms British Library Add. 26964)

verses.translation: And it came to pass{H1961}, when Yeshua{H3442} finished{H3615} commanding{H6680} his twelve{H8147}{H6240} disciples{H8527}, he passed on{H5674} from there{H8033} and commanded them{H6680} to teach{H3925} and to reprove{H3198} in their cities{H5892}.

one_way_hebrew: ולהוכיח (H3198, yakach) — 'to reprove': the Torah's own command word, הוכח תוכיח את עמיתך (Lev 19:17), and the work of the prophets (Isa 2:4). Greek Matthew has 'to teach and to preach (κηρύσσειν)'; the Hebrew pairs teaching with covenant reproof.
greek_deviations: In Greek Matthew 11:1 Jesus himself departs 'to teach and to preach in their cities.' The Hebrew reads ויצום — 'and he COMMANDED THEM to teach and to reprove in their cities': the disciples are sent to do the work, continuing the commissioning of ch. 10.
textual_notes: Shem Tov's own section heading פרק מ״ז (Perek 47) begins here.
The scan reads ויעבור ('and he passed on'); the circulating transcription's ויעבוד ('and he served') is a ד/ר typo, corrected here.
Howard's apparatus (11:1): ויצום] ויצא D ('and he went out').

verses.translation: And Yochanan{H3110}, while he was{H1961} imprisoned{H8610}, heard{H8085} of the work{H4639} of Yeshua{H3442}, and he sent{H7971} two{H8147} of his disciples{H8527}

one_way_hebrew: תפוס (H8610, taphas) — 'seized, in custody,' the arrest verb of Jer 37:13-14 (the seizing of Jeremiah the prophet); the imprisoned prophet hears and sends — Jeremiah's situation retold.
מעשה יש״ו — 'the WORK of Yeshua,' singular מעשה (H4639), where Greek has τὰ ἔργα ('the works'): Hebrew idiom treats the deeds as one work.
textual_notes: Howard's apparatus (11:2): שנים] + עשר EF (?) — mss EF apparently read 'his TWELVE disciples.'

verses.translation: to say{H559} to him: Are you{H859} he{H1931} who is destined{H6264} to come{H935}, or shall we hope{H6960} for another{H312}?

one_way_hebrew: נקוה (H6960, qavah) — 'hope, wait expectantly': the verb of Gen 49:18 (לישועתך קויתי יהוה, 'I have waited for thy salvation, YHWH') and Isa 25:9 ('we have waited for him, and he will save us'). The Baptizer's question is asked in the Tanakh's salvation-waiting verb; Greek προσδοκῶμεν ('expect') is flat anticipation.
העתיד לבא — 'the one destined to come': עתיד (H6264), the same 'destined' idiom the discourse of ch. 24 uses (24:6).
textual_notes: Howard's apparatus (11:3): האתה] אתה A.

verses.translation: And Yeshua{H3442} answered{H6030} them: Go{H1980} and tell{H5046} Yochanan{H3110} that which you have seen{H7200} and that which you have heard{H8085}:

greek_deviations: Greek Matthew has 'the things which ye hear and see' — hearing first, present tense. The Hebrew reads 'that which you have SEEN and that which you have HEARD' — seeing first, completed: the messengers report accomplished fact.
textual_notes: Howard's apparatus (11:4): את] omit A.

verses.translation: The blind{H5787} see{H7200}, and the lame{H6455} walk{H1980}, and the lepers{H6879} are cleansed{H2891}, and the deaf{H2795} hear{H8085}, and the dead{H4191} live{H2416}, and the humble{H6035} are acquitted.

one_way_hebrew: The catalogue is Isaiah's in Isaiah's own words: עורים and חרשים and פסחים are the very nouns of Isa 35:5-6 ('then the eyes of the blind shall be opened, and the ears of the deaf... then shall the lame man leap'), and ענוים is Isa 61:1's own word ('to bring good news to the humble — לבשר ענוים'). The answer to Yochanan is a mosaic of the signs Isaiah assigned to the day of God's coming.

The reading of mss EF, מתבשרים — 'are given good-news' (בשר, H1309) — is Isa 61:1's exact verb, the reading behind Greek εὐαγγελίζονται. Whichever reading is original, both live inside Hebrew Scripture; the Greek only translates.
translation_notes: מתפשרים — hitpael of the rabbinic verb פשר: 'have their case settled, are released, acquitted' (Howard: 'the poor are acquitted'). Mss EF read מתבשרים ('are given good-news'), one letter apart (ב/פ).

והחיים מתים — as printed, the base ms transposes the words ('the living... dead'); mss ABDEF read והמתים חיים ('the dead live'), the sense required by the Isaiah catalogue (Isa 26:19, 'thy dead shall live') and given by Howard's English ('the dead are revived'). The translation follows the sense; the words stand as the base prints.
textual_notes: Howard's apparatus (11:5): והחיים מתים] והמתים חיים ABDEF; ופסחים] הפסחים F, והפסחים BDE; נטהרים] מטהרים EF; מתפשרים] מתבשרים EF.
The Vat. Ebr. 100 Hebrew Matthew lacks the dead-clause entirely, reading only '...the deaf ones hear, and the humble ones are preached to.'

verses.translation: And happy{H835} is he who is not perplexed{H943} in me.

one_way_hebrew: נבוך (H943, buk) — 'entangled, perplexed': Pharaoh's word for Israel, נבכים הם בארץ ('they are entangled in the land,' Exod 14:3; cf. Joel 1:18). Greek σκανδαλισθῇ ('caused to stumble') is a different picture: the Hebrew blesses the one who does not lose his way in confusion over the Mashiach.
textual_notes: Howard's apparatus (11:6): ואשרי...בי] ואשר לא יהיה נכון בי EFG (?) ('who is not established in me').

verses.translation: And it came to pass{H1961}, as they were going{H1980}, Yeshua{H3442} began{H2490} to speak{H1696} to the crowds{H2267} about Yochanan{H3110}: What{H4100} did you go out{H3318} into the wilderness{H4057} to see{H7200} — a reed{H7070} cast about{H7993} by the wind{H7307}?

one_way_hebrew: קנה (H7070) — the shaken reed of 1 Kgs 14:15 ('as a reed is shaken in the water') and the bruised reed of Isa 42:3; מושלכת (H7993) — 'flung about.' The scene-word חבורות (H2267, 'companies') is native rabbinic Hebrew for the gathered crowds.
textual_notes: Howard's apparatus (11:7): ויהי המה הולכים] omit A; אל] את A; מיוחנן] ביוחנן B; יצאתם] + לראות A.

verses.translation: Or what did you go out{H3318} to see{H7200} — did you think{H2803} that Yochanan{H3110} was a man{H120} clothed{H3847} in noble{H7227} garments{H899}? Behold{H2009}, the wearers{H3847} of noble garments are in the houses{H1004} of kings{H4428}.

translation_notes: בגדים רבים — literally 'garments of the great ones' (רבים as in רב, 'chief, noble'); Howard renders 'noble garments.' Greek has μαλακά ('soft things') — a different word entirely.
textual_notes: Howard's apparatus (11:8): אדם] omit D; לבוש] לובש ADEFG; רבים 2°] הרבים A, omit G.

verses.translation: If so, what did you go out{H3318} to see{H7200} — a prophet{H5030}? In truth{H571} I say{H559} to you that this one{H2088} is greater{H1419} than a prophet{H5030}.

translation_notes: א״כ — the ms abbreviates אם כן ('if so') with gershayim, a native Hebrew scribal habit running through the whole text (cf. כ״ש at 12:12).

verses.translation: This is he{H2088} of whom it is written{H3789}: Behold{H2009}, I am sending{H7971} my messenger{H4397}, and he will clear{H6437} a way{H1870} before me{H6440}.

one_way_hebrew: The verse quotes Mal 3:1 in Malachi's own consonants: הנני שלח מלאכי ופנה דרך לפני — 'he will clear the way before ME,' YHWH speaking. Greek Matthew alters the citation to 'he shall prepare THY way before THEE' (τὴν ὁδόν σου ἔμπροσθέν σου), re-aiming the pronoun. A translator working from the Greek would have reproduced the Greek's 'thy way'; this text carries the Hebrew Bible's own wording untouched — the quotation only a Hebrew hand quoting Hebrew Scripture would write.
מלאכי (H4397) — 'my messenger,' which is also the prophet's own name (Malachi); in Hebrew the citation names its source in the very word.
textual_notes: Howard's apparatus (11:10): זהו] זה A; שולח] + לכם AE; לפני] omit G.

verses.translation: Again{H5750} Yeshua{H3442} said{H559} to his disciples{H8527}: In truth{H571} I speak{H1696} to you — among all{H3605} those born{H3206} of women{H802} there has not arisen{H6965} one greater{H1419} than Yochanan{H3110} the Immerser{H2881}.

one_way_hebrew: ילדי הנשים — 'born of women,' Job's idiom for frail mankind (ילוד אשה, Job 14:1; 15:14; 25:4).
המטביל — 'the Immerser,' from טבל (H2881), the verb of Naaman's sevenfold immersion (2 Kgs 5:14) and of Lev 14's cleansing rites: a native Hebrew agent-noun, not a transliteration of βαπτιστής.
greek_deviations: THE VERSE ENDS HERE. The Shem Tov text lacks the entire second half of Greek 11:11 — 'notwithstanding, he that is least in the kingdom of heaven is greater than he.' Howard records no variant supplying it in any of the nine mss; the text runs straight into v. 12, 'From his days until now...' In the Hebrew, Yochanan's greatness stands unqualified, and the following sentence turns at once to what has happened to the kingdom since his days. The Vat. Ebr. 100 Hebrew Matthew carries only a truncated remnant of the clause ('And the smallest of the heavenly kingdom —') that breaks off into v. 12 — in the Hebrew tradition the clause was unstable or absent; in the Greek it is fixed.
textual_notes: Shem Tov's own section heading פרק מ״ח (Perek 48) begins here.
Howard's apparatus (11:11): דובר] אומר AH.

verses.translation: From his days{H3117} until{H5704} now{H6258} the kingdom{H4438} of heaven{H8064} has been oppressed{H6231}, and they tear{H7167} it.

greek_deviations: Greek 11:12 reads 'the kingdom of heaven suffereth violence (βιάζεται), and the violent take it by force (ἁρπάζουσιν)' — seizure. The Hebrew reads עשוקה — 'OPPRESSED, defrauded' (עשק, H6231), the covenant word for grinding down the poor (Lev 19:13; Jer 22:3) — and קורעים אותה, 'they TEAR it': קרע (H7167) is the verb by which the kingdom is torn from Saul (1 Sam 15:28) and from Solomon (1 Kgs 11:11-13). In Hebrew the sentence carries the Samuel-Kings picture: the kingdom rent by the unworthy — not stormed by the eager.
textual_notes: Howard's apparatus (11:12): עד] ועד G; שמים] omit G; עשוקה] + והנבלים (spelled והנבילים in part of the mss) BDEFGH and A — 'and the worthless ones tear it'; Howard renders '(and senseless persons) have been rending it.'

verses.translation: For all{H3605} the prophets{H5030} and the Torah{H8451} spoke{H1696} concerning{H5921} Yochanan{H3110}.

greek_deviations: Greek Matthew reads 'all the prophets and the law prophesied UNTIL John' (ἕως Ἰωάννου) — a terminus, from which centuries have drawn the doctrine that the law ran out at John. The Hebrew preposition is על — they spoke CONCERNING Yochanan: he is the subject of their words (as v. 10 has just shown from Malachi), not the endpoint of their authority. Nothing in the Hebrew says the Torah ceased; it says the Torah testified.
textual_notes: Howard's apparatus (11:13): שכל] לכל DGH; והתורה] + כולה A ('and the whole Torah'); דברו] דברי D, דוברים H.

verses.translation: And if{H518} you are willing{H7521} to receive it{H6901}, he{H1931} is Eliyahu{H452} who is destined{H6264} to come{H935}.

one_way_hebrew: The sentence completes the Malachi frame opened at v. 10: 'Behold, I send you Eliyahu the prophet before the coming of the great and dreadful day of YHWH' (Mal 3:23). In Hebrew, vv. 10 and 14 are two halves of one prophet's book; in Greek they are two detached quotations.
textual_notes: The scan reads תרצו ('you are willing'); the circulating transcription's תרעו is a typo, corrected here.
אליה — the ms spells Eliyahu defectively (אליה); mss ABDG normalize to אליהו.
Howard's apparatus (11:14): לקבלו] + מלכות שמים B (?); אליה] אליהו ABDG.

verses.translation: Whoever has ears{H241} to hear{H8085}, let him hear{H8085}.

one_way_hebrew: The hearing formula of the prophets (Ezek 3:27, 'he that heareth, let him hear'); שמע carries both hearing and obeying, as in the Shema (Deut 6:4) — one verb doubled, אזנים לשמוע ישמע, exactly as at 13:9 and 13:43.

verses.translation: Again{H5750} Yeshua{H3442} said{H559}: This{H2088} generation{H1755} — I will liken it{H1819} to lads{H5288} sitting{H3427} in the market{H7784}, calling{H7121} one to another,

one_way_hebrew: שוק (H7784) — the market-street of Prov 7:8 and Song 3:2; אדמהו (H1819, damah) — 'I will liken it,' the prophets' own comparison verb (Hos 12:11, 'I have used similitudes').
textual_notes: Shem Tov's own section heading פרק מ״ט (Perek 49) begins here.
Howard's apparatus (11:16): אדמהו] אדמה DEFG.

verses.translation: and saying{H559}: We sang{H7891} to you and you did not dance{H7540}; we lamented{H5594} to you and you did not weep{H1058}.

one_way_hebrew: The mss' verb pair — רקדתם ('dance') and ספדנו ('lament') — is Qohelet's own pair: עת ספוד ועת רקוד, 'a time to mourn and a time to dance' (Eccl 3:4). The children's game runs on the Preacher's two times; Greek ὠρχήσασθε/ἐθρηνήσαμεν translates the pair without the echo.

The base ms garbles all three verbs by ד/ר interchange (שדנו for שרנו, דקדקתם for רקדתם, ספרנו for ספדנו) — dalet and resh being near-identical in Hebrew script. A copyist's confusion of ד and ר can only happen in a HEBREW transmission chain; a text freshly translated from Greek would not carry generations of inner-Hebrew copying errors.
translation_notes: The translation follows the majority mss, which Howard prints in parentheses: שרנו לכם ('we sang to you,' ABCDEF), רקדתם ('you danced,' ABEFG), ספדנו ('we lamented,' ABCDEF). The words stand as the base ms prints them.
textual_notes: Howard's apparatus (11:17): שדנו] שרנו לכם ABCDEF; דקדקתם] רקדתם ABEFG, מדתם D; ספרנו] ספדנו ABCDEF.

verses.translation: For{H3588} Yochanan{H3110} came{H935}, neither eating{H398} nor drinking{H8354}, and they say{H559} concerning him: He is seized{H270} by demons{H7700}.

one_way_hebrew: שדים (H7700, shedim) — Deut 32:17's word ('they sacrificed to shedim, not to God'; cf. Ps 106:37): the Torah's own name for the powers behind idolatry. Greek δαιμόνιον is the pagan loan-category; the Hebrew keeps Moses' word.
אחוז (H270, achaz) — 'seized, held fast' (אחוזי חרב, Song 3:8); possession pictured as being gripped.
textual_notes: Howard's apparatus (11:18): משדים] מהשדים A, השדים EF.

verses.translation: But the Son{H1121} of Man{H120} came{H935} to eat{H398} and to drink{H8354}, and one says{H559} concerning him: He is a glutton{H2151} and a drunkard{H5433}, and a friend{H157} of violent men{H6530} and sinners{H2400}. And the fools{H5530} judge{H8199} the wise{H2450}.

one_way_hebrew: זולל וסובא — 'a glutton and a drunkard': the exact word-pair of Deut 21:20, the parents' capital charge against the rebellious son (בננו זה... זולל וסבא). The generation indicts the Son of Man in the Torah's own formula for the son who will not hear — an irony that exists only in Hebrew; Greek φάγος καὶ οἰνοπότης translates the words and loses the statute.
פריצים (H6530) — 'violent men, robbers' (Ezek 7:22; Dan 11:14 בני פריצי עמך); Greek Matthew has τελωνῶν ('tax-collectors'). The Hebrew charge is harsher and Scriptural.
greek_deviations: The verse closes 'and the fools judge the wise' (והסכלים שופטים לחכמים) where Greek Matthew has 'wisdom is justified of her children' (ἐδικαιώθη ἡ σοφία ἀπὸ τῶν τέκνων αὐτῆς). The Hebrew is a plain verdict on the whole exchange: the generation that condemned both Yochanan and the Son of Man is folly passing sentence on wisdom (Eccl 10:6, 'folly is set in great dignity').
textual_notes: Howard's apparatus (11:19): האדם] אדם AG; ואומר] ואומרים ABEFG.
The scan reads ואומר עליו ('and one says concerning him'); the circulating transcription dropped עליו, restored here.

verses.translation: Then{H227} Yeshua{H3442} began{H2490} to curse{H7043} the cities in which some of his signs{H226} had been done{H6213} and which had not turned{H7725} in repentance{H8666}.

one_way_hebrew: חזרו בתשובה — 'turned in repentance': the rabbinic Hebrew idiom for repentance (teshuvah), used throughout this text (cf. v. 21) where Greek has the bare verb μετενόησαν. A translator from Greek renders a verb; a Hebrew author writes his community's living idiom.
translation_notes: הנערים — the base ms reads 'the LADS' (its eye assimilating to v. 16's נערים); all other mss (ABCDEFG) read הערים, 'the CITIES,' which the woes that follow require (Chorazin, Beit Saidah, Kefar Nachum). Howard: 'to curse (the cities in which) his signs were done.' The translation follows the majority; the words stand as the base prints.
textual_notes: Shem Tov's own section heading פרק חמשים (Perek 50) begins here; the circulating transcription had run the heading onto the end of v. 19, where the scan prints it as a heading between vv. 19 and 20.
Howard's apparatus (11:20): התחיל] אתחיל G; הנערים] הערים ABCDEFG; שנעשו] + בהן A, + בהם BDEFG.

verses.translation: Woe{H337} to you, Chorazin, and woe{H337} to you, Beit{H1004} Saidah! For if in Tyre{H6865} and Sodom{H5467} — in the foreign tongue{H3937}, Tirao deter or Sedoma — had been done{H6213} the signs{H226} that were done in you, they would have turned in repentance{H8666} in that{H1931} time{H2165}, in sackcloth{H8242} and ashes{H665}.

one_way_hebrew: בשק ואפר — 'in sackcloth and ashes': the Hebrew penitence formula (Esth 4:3; Dan 9:3; Jonah 3:6 — Nineveh's own repentance, the counter-example to these towns). Greek ἐν σάκκῳ καὶ σποδῷ translates it.
greek_deviations: The Hebrew pairs Tyre with SODOM, not Sidon: vv. 21-24 build one continuous Sodom-argument — 'Tyre and Sodom' (v. 21), 'easier for Tyre and Sodom' (v. 22), Sodom against Kefar Nachum (v. 23), 'the land of Sodom in the day of judgment' (v. 24). Greek Matthew reads 'Tyre and Sidon' in vv. 21-22 and brings in Sodom only at v. 23-24; ms G assimilates to the Greek with וצדון ('and Sidon'). The Vat. Ebr. 100 Hebrew Matthew likewise reads 'Tsor and Tsidon.'

Like the evangeli gloss of 24:14, the text glosses its own Hebrew place-names with a vernacular equivalent — לעז טיראו דיטיר או סדומה (Howard: 'Tirao deter or Sidomah') — an annotation for readers who knew the names in church language, intelligible only if the Hebrew text is the host and the foreign words the visitors.
textual_notes: The scan reads בזמן ההוא ('in that time'); the circulating transcription's מזמן is a typo, corrected here.
Howard's apparatus (11:21): וסדום] וצדון G; בצור] בפור EF; בית] בת DG; the vernacular gloss varies across the mss (טיר וסודומה A; טיר או שדומה BDG).

verses.translation: Amen{H543}, I say{H559} to you: it will be easier{H7031} for Tyre{H6865} and Sodom{H5467}, indeed{H403}.

greek_deviations: The base text ends the sentence at אכן ('indeed'), leaving the comparison to be completed by v. 24; mss ADG read מכם ('than YOU'), B מכאן, EF מכך, filling it out as in the Greek — Howard renders '(than for you).' The base also lacks 'in the day of judgment' here; the Hebrew reserves it for the climax at v. 24.
textual_notes: Howard's apparatus (11:22): אכן] מכם ADG, מכאן B, מכך EF; וסדום] ולסדום AB.

verses.translation: And you{H859}, Kefar{H3723} Nachum{H5151}: if to the heavens{H8064} you rise{H5927}, from there{H8033} you will be brought down{H3381}. For if in Sodom{H5467} had been done{H6213} some of the signs{H226} that were done in you, perhaps{H194} she would have remained{H7604}. Unto{H5704} Sheol{H7585} you will be brought down{H3381}.

one_way_hebrew: אם לשמים תעלה משם תורד — the taunt-song of Isa 14:13-15 against the king of Babylon ('I will ascend into heaven... yet thou shalt be brought down to Sheol') and Obad 4 ('though thou set thy nest among the stars, thence will I bring thee down'), in the prophets' own verbs עלה and ירד, ending on שאול by name. Greek ᾅδης stands in for Sheol; the Hebrew has the name itself, and with it the whole Isaiah 14 scene.
textual_notes: Howard's apparatus (11:23): ms A rearranges toward the Greek — עד שאול after משם, and היום הזה ('this day') for שאול תורד, ending 'perhaps she would have remained until this day'; תורד 1°] תוריד B. The Vat. Ebr. 100 Hebrew Matthew likewise ends 'they would still have done repentance until this day.'

verses.translation: Amen{H543}, I say{H559} to you that it will be easier{H7031} for the land{H776} of Sodom{H5467} in the day{H3117} of judgment{H1779} than for you.

one_way_hebrew: יום הדין — 'the day of the din (judgment)': the rabbinic Hebrew name for the final judgment, native to a Hebrew author's eschatology; Greek ἡμέρᾳ κρίσεως translates it.
textual_notes: The scan reads לארץ סדום ליום הדין; the circulating transcription's סדות הדין is a typo, corrected here.
Howard's apparatus (11:24): קל] omit G; יהיה] תהיה ABDG.

verses.translation: At that{H1931} time{H6256} Yeshua{H3442} was exalted{H7311} and said{H559}: Praised be{H7623} the creator{H1254} of heaven{H8064} and earth{H776}, for you have hidden{H5641} these{H428} words{H1697} from the wise{H2450} and the understanding{H995} and have revealed{H1540} them to the lowly{H6041}.

one_way_hebrew: The prayer is a Hebrew berakhah in form: ישתבח — the hitpael of שבח (H7623) that opens the synagogue doxology (Yishtabach) — addressed to בורא שמים, the creator-epithet of Isa 42:5 (בורא השמים). Greek 'I thank thee (ἐξομολογοῦμαί σοι), Lord of heaven and earth' recasts a blessing as a thanksgiving and 'creator' as 'Lord.'

מהחכמים והנבונים — 'from the wise and the understanding': the fixed pair of Deut 1:13 and Deut 4:6 (חכמים ונבונים). And לעניים — 'to the lowly' (עני, H6041; most mss לענוים) — is Isa 61:1's own word, where Greek has νηπίοις ('babes'). The whole sentence runs on Tanakh word-pairs the Greek only translates.

נתרומם (H7311, rum) — 'was exalted, lifted up' — where Greek Matthew has ἀποκριθείς ('answered'). Mss ABDE add ברוח ('in the spirit'), G ברוח הקדש — agreeing with Luke 10:21, 'rejoiced in the spirit,' against Greek Matthew.
translation_notes: The base ms writes אני both before and after ישתבח (ואומר אני ישתבח אני בורא — a dittography); all other mss omit the first אני, and ms A reads אבי ('my Father') for the second: 'Praised be my Father, creator of heaven and earth.' Howard: 'Be praised (my Father) creator of heaven and earth.' The translation renders the sentence without the doubled pronoun.
textual_notes: Shem Tov's own section heading פרק נ״א (Perek 51) begins here.
Howard's apparatus (11:25): ישו] + ברוח ABDE, + ברוח הקדש G; אני 1°] omit ABCDEFG; אני 2°] אבי A; שמים] השמים ABCDEF; והארץ] וארץ FG; לעניים] לענוים in part of the mss.

verses.translation: Truly{H551}, for so{H3651} it is upright{H3477} before you{H6440}, my Father{H1}.

one_way_hebrew: ישר לפניך — 'upright before you': the idiom of doing הישר בעיני יהוה ('what is right in the eyes of YHWH,' Deut 12:25). Greek εὐδοκία ('good pleasure') is a different category; the Hebrew grounds the Father's choice in uprightness.
textual_notes: Howard's apparatus (11:26): אמנם] + אבי ABDEFGH; אבי] omit ABDEFGH — the other mss move 'my Father' to the head of the sentence ('Truly, my Father, for so it is upright before you'); ישר] יש A, רצוי H ('pleasing').

verses.translation: Everything{H3605} has been given{H5414} to me by my Father{H1}; and there is none{H369} who knows{H5234} the Son{H1121} except the Father{H1} alone{H905}, and the Father — there is none{H369} who knows{H5234} him except the Son{H1121}, and he to whom the Son wishes{H7521} to reveal him{H1540}.

one_way_hebrew: מכיר (H5234, nakar) — relational recognition, the knowing of a face (Ruth 2:10,19; Gen 27:23), not bare information; the Father-Son knowing is stated in the vocabulary of kinship recognition.
בלבד (H905) — 'ALONE': the same word this text uses at 24:36, 'except the Father alone.' The two sayings answer each other across the book in one Hebrew idiom.
textual_notes: Howard's apparatus (11:27): הכל] כל H; נתון] נתן B; מאת אבי] מאבי H; את] omit GH; אלא 1°] כי אם G; אלא 2°] כי אם H; בלבד] לבד C, omit H; ולאשר ירצה] ולמי שירצה H; ירצה] omit EF.

verses.translation: Come{H935} to him, all{H3605} you weary{H3023} and bearers{H5375} of toil{H5999}, and I will help{H5826} you to bear{H5375} your yoke{H5923}.

greek_deviations: The promise differs from the Greek at its center: Greek reads 'and I will give you REST' (κἀγὼ ἀναπαύσω ὑμᾶς); the Hebrew reads ואני אעזור אתכם לשאת עולכם — 'and I will HELP you to BEAR your yoke.' The yoke is not lifted off; it is shouldered together. Rest comes in the next verse (מרגוע, v. 29) as the result. The picture is Num 11:17 — the seventy who 'bear the burden of the people with thee, that thou bear it not thyself alone.'
translation_notes: בואו אליו — the base ms reads 'come to HIM' (a third-person frame, as if quoting the invitation); mss AB read אלי, 'to me,' and Howard's English follows them ('Come unto me') against his own base text.
textual_notes: Howard's apparatus (11:28): בואו] לכו H; אליו] אלי AB; לשאת] לשנות DG.

verses.translation: Take up{H5375} my yoke{H5923} as your yoke, and learn{H3925} from me, and you will know{H5234} that I am humble{H6041} and good{H2896} and pure{H1249} of heart{H3824}, and you will find{H4672} rest{H4771} for your souls{H5315}.

one_way_hebrew: ותמצאו מרגוע לנפשותיכם — Jer 6:16 verbatim: 'ask for the old paths, where is the good way, and walk therein, and ye shall find rest for your souls (ומצאו מרגוע לנפשכם).' מרגוע (H4771) occurs in Scripture only there; a Hebrew author reaches for Jeremiah's rare word, and with it Jeremiah's meaning — the yoke to be taken up is the old paths, the good way. Greek ἀνάπαυσιν translates the word and loses the address.

ובר הלבב — 'and pure of heart': Ps 24:4's temple-entry qualification (נקי כפים ובר לבב). Greek Matthew has 'meek and lowly in heart' with no purity term; the Hebrew speaker claims the Psalm's clean heart.
עני (H6041) — 'humble, lowly': Zech 9:9's royal word (עני ורוכב על חמור, 'lowly, and riding upon an ass').
translation_notes: צאו עולי עולכם — as the base prints, 'go out(?) my yoke your yoke': garbled. Mss AB read שאו ('take up') for צאו, and BDEFG read עליכם ('upon you') for עולכם — 'take my yoke upon you,' as in the Greek. Howard: '(Take) my yoke as your yoke.' The translation follows the sense; the words stand as the base prints.
textual_notes: Howard's apparatus (11:29): צאו] שאו AB; צאו...עולכם] omit C (haplography); עולכם] עלכם A, עליכם BDEFG; הלבב] לבב B; לנפשותיכם] לנפשותכם A.

verses.translation: For my yoke is gentle{H7390}, and my burden{H4853} is light{H7031}.

one_way_hebrew: עול and משא — yoke and burden: the pair of Isa 10:27, 'his burden (סבלו) shall be taken away from off thy shoulder, and his yoke (עלו) from off thy neck.' משא (H4853) is also the prophets' word for an oracle — the 'burden' a prophet carries; the speaker's burden is light.
translation_notes: The base ms opens the verse with bare רק ('only'); mss BDEFG prefix שעולי ('for my yoke is...'), A reads ושעולי and רך ('soft, gentle') for רק — a ק/ך final-form slip. The full sentence, 'for my yoke is gentle and my burden light,' is what Howard renders: '(because my yoke is soft) and my burden light.' The words stand as the base prints; the tag follows the sense רך.
textual_notes: Howard's apparatus (11:30): at the beginning, + שעולי BDEFG, + ושעולי A; רק] רך A.

chapter_notes.summary: Matthew 11 in the Shem Tov Hebrew differs from the Greek at its most quoted lines. (1) 11:11 ENDS at 'there has not arisen one greater than Yochanan the Immerser' — the Shem Tov text lacks the entire 'he that is least in the kingdom of heaven is greater than he' clause, in all nine of Howard's mss; Vat. Ebr. 100 carries only a truncated remnant of it. (2) 11:13 reads 'all the prophets and the Torah spoke CONCERNING (על) Yochanan' — not 'prophesied UNTIL John': the Hebrew makes Yochanan the subject of the Torah's testimony, not the terminus of its authority. (3) 11:10 quotes Mal 3:1 in Malachi's own consonants — ופנה דרך לפני, 'he will clear the way before ME' — where Greek Matthew re-points the pronouns ('thy way before thee'); v. 14 then completes Malachi with Eliyahu (Mal 3:23). (4) 11:12 reads 'the kingdom of heaven is OPPRESSED (עשוקה) and they TEAR it (קורעים)' — the verb of the kingdom torn from Saul (1 Sam 15:28) — not the Greek's 'suffers violence and the violent seize it.' (5) 11:21-24 pair Tyre with SODOM throughout (ms G assimilates to 'Sidon'), glossed in the vernacular (לעז 'Tirao deter o Sedoma') like the evangeli gloss of 24:14, and close on the rabbinic 'day of the din' (יום הדין). (6) 11:25 is a Hebrew berakhah — 'Praised be (ישתבח) the creator of heaven and earth' — with the Deut 1:13 pair 'wise and understanding' and Isa 61:1's 'lowly' (עניים) where Greek has 'babes'; mss add 'in the (holy) spirit,' agreeing with Luke 10:21. (7) 11:28 promises 'I will HELP you to BEAR your yoke' (not 'I will give you rest'), and 11:29 quotes Jer 6:16 verbatim (מרגוע לנפשותיכם — the old paths) and Ps 24:4 (בר הלבב, 'pure of heart'). (8) 11:19 indicts the Son of Man in Deut 21:20's own formula for the rebellious son (זולל וסובא) and closes 'the fools judge the wise.' (9) 11:5's catalogue is Isa 35:5-6 + Isa 61:1 in Isaiah's own nouns, with ms-variant מתבשרים = Isa 61:1's very verb. (10) The base ms shows inner-Hebrew copying history — ד/ר interchanges at 11:17 (שדנו/דקדקתם/ספרנו for שרנו/רקדתם/ספדנו), נערים for ערים at 11:20 — errors only a Hebrew transmission chain can produce. Shem Tov's own section divisions fall at vv. 1 (Perek 47), 11 (48), 16 (49), 20 (50), and 25 (51).
